problem: Frontier+VLM zero-shot ObjectNav systems collapse frontier candidates into scalar scores, stop on brittle single-frame detection thresholds, and use heuristic recovery that fails to prevent repeated false positives (cyclic deadlocks).
motivation: ObjectNav needs both good long-horizon exploration (where to go) and reliable termination (when to stop). Scalar scoring or text abstractions lose spatial structure such as connectivity and layout, and open-vocabulary detectors produce persistent false positives such as reflections, so a principled decision interface and uncertainty-aware commitment are needed.
key_idea: Represent frontiers as persistent-ID multimodal tokens presented to a VLM as a Set-of-Marks bundle for comparative reasoning, and replace threshold stopping with Bayesian SPRT evidence accumulation plus an energy-field instance-level quarantine of rejected targets.
insight: Ablations on HM3Dv1 show that VLM token reasoning matters most (no brain: -13.9 pp SR, from 63.2 to 49.3), followed by priors (-12.8 pp) and memory (-9.0 pp). Sequential commitment and quarantine (replacing them with single-frame stopping) cost a further 4.8 pp SR. The gains come from preserving spatial structure in the VLM interface and from decoupling exploration from commitment. The stop-chain ablation merges SPRT and quarantine, so their individual contributions are not separated.
method: Tokenized frontier representation: a FrontierTracker matches newly extracted free-unknown frontier components to existing tokens by spatial nearest neighbour, so IDs persist across map updates. Each token stores distance, semantic priors, memory signals and selection history.

Set-of-Marks bundle + VLM comparative reasoning: the VLM (Qwen3-VL-8B) receives an RGB frame with detections, a BEV occupancy map with indexed frontier tokens, and a feature table, then selects a frontier with a confidence. It is triggered by events (about 52 calls per episode) and runs asynchronously.
Geometric UCB fallback: when VLM confidence is below a threshold or reasoning is unavailable, choose argmax of the running mean semantic score plus β·sqrt(ln t/(n_i+1)), with β=1.4.

Spatial and semantic memory: a SpatialMemoryBank gives repulsive/attractive signals on visited poses and detects short-term cycles with a sliding window. A FAISS-based SemanticMemoryBank retrieves past observation embeddings into the VLM prompt.

SPRT-based commitment: a log-odds belief Λ_t = max(0, Λ_{t-1} + λdet + λgeo + λvlm + λqua) accumulates YOLOE detection confidence, depth-geometric consistency, and a VLM crop verification. STOP fires when Λ ≥ Λcommit, and the threshold is raised when co-occurrence cues are absent.

Instance-level quarantine: when a hypothesized target anchor is rejected, a negative Gaussian energy field is placed at its BEV projection. Its value at the current hypothesis location is added as λqua, suppressing repeated commitment to the same false instance.

setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (with pose) building a 5 cm/cell occupancy map
setting.action_space: low-level motion primitives + STOP, with frontier selection as the high-level decision

numbers.extra: HM3Dv1; success radius 1.0 m, 500 steps; deterministic seed=0

numbers_note: The paper labels HM3Dv1 and HM3Dv2 evaluation sets as 'validation'. Ablation variants (Table II) were not added separately, except the Full row.
results: FaT reaches 63.2% SR / 0.348 SPL on HM3Dv1 and 79.1% SR / 0.401 SPL on HM3Dv2, beating ApexNav (59.6/.330 and 76.2/.380). On MP3D it has the best SPL (0.196) but lower SR (41.8) than WMNav (45.4), all with an open-source 8B VLM.
limitations: Depends on open-vocabulary detector quality; weakly represented categories give little evidence, and visually aliased objects (couch vs bed) still trigger wrong stops.
Path inefficiency in large open-plan scenes with many frontiers, and near-target timeouts when evidence is insufficient.
Extra runtime versus the geometric baseline (231 s vs 148 s per episode on an A100) and no real-robot validation.
